aboutMe.highlighted_title: Occupational Therapist and Art Therapy Practitioner

aboutMePage.paragraph:
Under the slogan RUA, I am Tina Zadravec, Master of Art Therapy and a graduate occupational therapist. With decades of experience, I connect knowledge from university studies and additional professional training to ensure an individualized approach and treatment for each person.

I co-create moments when users say: "I haven’t had so many ideas and information about the possibilities that exist in a long time!"
We help people rebuild the belief that they, too, can perform everyday activities that have long seemed impossible.
 
Within occupational therapy, we work in the field of [re]habilitation of individuals with neurological and musculoskeletal difficulties, as well as challenges in mental health. We value knowledge and wisdom and thoughtfully introduce new approaches and therapeutic tools into our work. We also collaborate with professionals from abroad.
We are active members of the Chamber of Occupational Therapists of Slovenia and the Slovenian Association of Art Therapists.

items.title: Occupational therapy for children and adolescents

elderlyHero.subtitle: for older adults
elderlyHero.description:
Occupational therapy is a healthcare profession, and an occupational therapist is a healthcare professional who encourages individuals to engage in meaningful everyday activities. Within occupational therapy, we focus on improving or maintaining health in the areas of bodily functions and structures, as well as mental health.

Our shared goals are to carry out activities that promote health, well-being, and the most successful performance of prioritized activities. As an occupational therapist, I am also here to guide you through the components needed to perform activities in the areas of basic daily living — such as independent washing, dressing, and eating.

We will also look at participation in broader daily activities, assess environmental risk factors, work on fall prevention, and provide advice on adapting the home for greater safety. With the individual, we will discuss the use of orthotic and medical-technical aids, and with family members, we will talk about supportive technology that can help the person maintain independence.

youngerHero.subtitle: for children and adolescents
youngerHero.description:
Pediatric occupational therapy targets different age groups of children and adolescents. In the first year, it helps infants with handling, independent feeding and swallowing, the development of play and fine motor skills, and the development of quality movement in the form of gross motor skills.

Within occupational therapy, children develop independence in various areas.

featuresOdrasli.title: Don't miss ...
featuresOdrasli.subtitle: Benefits of occupational therapy
featuresOdrasli.description: Occupational therapy brings many benefits to your health and quality of life. With an individually tailored approach, we help you achieve greater independence in everyday activities, improve physical and mental well-being, and actively participate in society. Discover the key benefits that occupational therapy can bring to your life.

items.name: Art therapy support
items.description: Art therapy guides a person through the process of expression and creation. Through music, theater/drama, or visual art therapy approaches, it encourages self-expression, physical and mental well-being, and personal growth. Our focus is on the experience itself, not the final product.

items.name: Neuromuscular taping
items.description: A technique that influences the musculoskeletal, vascular, lymphatic, and neurological systems. It uses (de)compressive stimuli by applying a self-adhesive elastic tape to support the body’s natural healing.

items.name: Occupational therapy with Montessori elements
items.description: When working with people with dementia, it is crucial to understand the individual beyond the diagnosis, including their abilities, interests, and life experience. Respecting their personal, cultural, and social background enables a supportive environment that nurtures independence and meaningful participation. The Montessori approach to dementia and ageing is grounded in the principles of self-respect, choice, and active contribution to the community.

items.name: Bobath concept
items.description: A therapeutic approach to the (re)habilitation of neurological conditions, focused on the quality of movement and activity performance. The emphasis is on transferring learned skills into everyday activities and occupations.

featuresOtroci.title: Don't miss ...
featuresOtroci.subtitle: Benefits of occupational therapy
featuresOtroci.description: Occupational therapy offers many advantages for a child's health and quality of life. With an individually tailored approach, we help them gain greater independence in daily activities, boost physical and emotional well-being, and participate more confidently in their surroundings. Discover the key benefits occupational therapy can bring to your child.

items.name: Art therapy support
items.description: Art therapy guides the child through a process of expression and creation. Using music, theatre/drama, or visual art approaches, it encourages self-expression, emotional balance, and personal growth.

items.name: Neuromuscular taping
items.description: A technique that supports the musculoskeletal, vascular, lymphatic, and neurological systems. By applying gentle (de)compressive stimuli with elastic tape, we promote the body's natural healing and alignment.

items.name: Occupational therapy with Montessori elements
items.description: Guided by the principle "Help me do it myself," the child gains confidence, develops sensory awareness, and discovers joy in learning. Purposeful materials encourage independence, while learning from mistakes shows them how to recognise and correct missteps.

items.name: Bobath concept
items.description: A therapeutic approach to the (re)habilitation of neurological conditions that focuses on quality of movement and activity. It emphasises helping the child transfer newly learned skills into everyday routines and meaningful play.

home.heroKicker: for the young and the old
home.heroText: Rehabilitation and arts therapies for children and elderly — with compassion, presence and expertise we walk beside you toward greater independence and quality of life.
home.heroImageAlt: Occupational therapist during an activity with a child
home.introText: Occupational therapy is a health profession that encourages each person to engage in the everyday activities meaningful to them. It focuses on improving and maintaining physical function, mental health and independence — from a baby's first movements to dignified ageing.

children.title: Pediatric occupational therapy
children.lead: Tailored to different age groups. In the first year it supports babies with handling, feeding and swallowing, play, fine motor skills and quality of movement.
items: Build fine motor skills, object manipulation and upper-limb coordination.
Develop graphomotor skills — grip, drawing and writing.
Strengthen eye–hand coordination for play and school skills.
Master daily activities: dressing, brushing teeth, feeding.
Learn to use medical-technical aids and adaptations.

adults.title: Occupational therapy for elderly
adults.lead: We focus on improving and maintaining physical function, mental health and independence in the daily activities that matter most.
adults.listTitle: Occupational therapy is for someone who:
items: Is recovering from injury or surgery and wants to keep muscle function.
Is facing central nervous system injury (stroke, brain injury).
Faces movement challenges due to age-related changes.
Lives with chronic illness (Parkinson's, multiple sclerosis).
Is facing cognitive changes and wants to keep daily independence.
Needs home adaptations to prevent falls.

childrenPage.title: Occupational therapy
intro: Pediatric occupational therapy focuses on different age groups of children and adolescents.
In the first year it helps babies with handling, independent feeding and swallowing, play and fine motor development, and building quality of movement through gross motor skills.

Furthermore, within occupational therapy — which is individually tailored — children develop independence in cognitive, motor and social areas, such as learning everyday self-care activities [feeding, personal hygiene, dressing] and the possible use of aids for independence.

followUp: Sessions stimulate physical and cognitive development. With elements of sensory integration we recognise, regulate, organise and integrate sensations and senses in the body for effective functioning in the environment.

odrasliFor.header: Occupational therapy is for those, who:
list: Are recovering from musculoskeletal injuries or surgeries (e.g. hip, shoulder or arm fractures) and want to regain or maintain muscle function.
Are facing central nervous system injuries (e.g. stroke, cerebral palsy, spinal cord or brain injuries, meningitis, ALS).
Are experiencing movement challenges due to age-related changes (e.g. reduced strength, mobility and balance).
Live with chronic illnesses (e.g. Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis, Huntington's disease).
Experience cognitive changes (e.g. dementia, Alzheimer's disease, mild cognitive impairment), where the goal is to maintain daily independence.
Have difficulties with daily activities (e.g. dressing, personal hygiene, cooking and shopping).
Need adjustments to their home environment (e.g. aids, safe room layouts to prevent falls, bathroom modifications).
Want to use medical-technical aids but are looking for ideas on how to use them.
Live in a home environment and want to maintain as much independence and quality of life as possible.
Face social and psychological challenges (loneliness, loss of motivation or depression), where occupational therapy can offer meaningful activities and support.

otrociFor.header: With occupational therapy at RUA, children can:
list: Strengthen the intrinsic muscles of the hand for fine motor skills, object manipulation, and upper limb coordination.
Build fine motor abilities for grasping and releasing toys, developing pincer grasp, and improving drawing and writing skills.
Improve eye-hand coordination for play or school skills.
Master basic daily activities such as dressing, tooth brushing, and eating independently.
Receive guidance on specific aids that support movement, handwriting, putting on socks, and more.
otrociFor.extra:
Sessions encourage progress in both physical and cognitive development. With elements of sensory integration we recognize, regulate, organize, and integrate sensations in the body for effective participation in the environment.
We actively involve parents or guardians in therapy so they can transfer what they observe to the home environment. We understand the importance of 24-hour positioning.
We advise on possible adjustments in preschool, school, or home settings and on the use of therapeutic aids.
